utterances.text: All the times I provided were estimates. I only said exactly when we arrived at Ovcara because I knew that. And as for the time of departure, I oriented myself by the amount of light. And I can accept it was at about a quarter to 5.00 in the afternoon, if that's what science says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that while you were outside the hangar, a group of JNA officers drove in at Ovcara; there were three or four of them. And you gave us a more detailed account of the incident involving the boy whose mother interceded for him to be saved from the hangar. You mentioned several names, or you were unable to recall the names. But can you remember - because we don't have it here on the record - do you remember the rank of the person who said, I saved this child? Did he mention his rank?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: I remember he mentioned colonel. That's from my memory. He could have been lieutenant-colonel, but a colonel was certainly mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed that you mentioned this same rank of colonel in your previous testimony as well. You mentioned names Ivankovic, Ivanovic, Jovanovic. You were not sure about his surname. I'd like to know if the name Kijanovic rings a bell?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: To be quite honest with you, I heard that surname somewhere, but I can't be sure now. I told you about Vukovar, and I did some research and reading myself later. That surname is somewhere in my head, but I can't place it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During your time at Ovcara, you saw certain vehicles coming and going, standing there. Could you give us some details, if you can remember, what kind of vehicles were they?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the vehicles were military vehicles. As for other types, right now I can't remember. I know, at any rate, there were different types of military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned -- in fact, can you tell me now while you were at Ovcara, that is to say before you left, you observed those officers who were there. You saw those military vehicles. Was that situation unchanged all the time while you were there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: The officers were there all the time. They oversaw the whole situation. They walked around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said a lot about this in your prior testimony, but let me ask you again: Do you have the impression that the officers who were present there had control over the situation? Did they issue any orders that were obeyed by all the others who were there?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: My main assertion in my testimony about that event was that the supervision, the organisational aspect and the planning aspect was totally in control of the Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA officers, and, of course, there were people there who executed, but the absolute control over that situation was in the hands of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There's perhaps one thing that remains unclear on the record. It's on page 22 when you spoke about leaving Ovcara. You said - at least that's what's on the record - there was somebody called Dr. Ivankovic. You were talking about his son. But was Dr. Ivankovic also in that bus?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was talking all the time about Dr. Ivankovic's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And since you mentioned the same surname also when you were talking about that colonel, that was neither Dr. Ivankovic nor his son?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a photograph, P1076, a photograph or a freeze of a soldier closing the hangar, and you said you had seen that man up at Ovcara. Were you able to see, did he have a rank?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember a rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And I noticed one other thing. On page 26, line 9, you mentioned in that context, although I don't believe it's on the record, a certain Safet from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Because the name is not recorded correctly. Could you explain once again who that Safet from Doboj was.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Muslim who was a volunteer, and whose ideology was that he was fighting for and saving Yugoslavia, and that's why he was a volunteer in Vukovar on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you P3005, which is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see that once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You identified this man whose face is encircled here. Can you see in the background these men who are also standing apparently wearing uniforms? Because you were put to some trouble earlier and today concerning the distinction between members of the JNA, the Chetniks, the Territorial Defence, et cetera. Can you tell me, from their appearance, how would you denote this man whose face is encircled as a member of a certain establishment or unit, regardless of what you later learned about him.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Look, while that all was going on, while Kinez was rescuing me, by the way he was dressed and his demeanour, I decided that he did not belong to the Yugoslav People's Army, that he was one of Seselj's Men. There is a reason why he was dressed like that, but I don't know that it's important now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you see these other two soldiers in the back, from your entire views and -- and ideas about this, how would you identify them? Where would you put him? In -- in which group?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Also somewhere in the JNA. I don't know whether they would be reservists or active duty, but they would be JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see 1D834, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll show you just one more picture in the same context. Look at these two soldiers. I think you can see their helmets. You can even see the emblems on their helmets, although it's not very clear. You can see something red on the helmets. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: I see it. But, to be quite honest, I am a bit colour-blind, so I have a problem with colours red and green. I see some kind of spot, though, a stain. I wouldn't talk about the right one because I can't see anything about the helmet. And the left one, I would put in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to that officer who told that woman that he had saved her child. Can you tell the Chamber -- you described his appearance, his height, and you said, among other things, that his hair was already grey.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean he was getting on in age?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, grey hair doesn't necessarily mean advanced age. Now that I'm 43, even 60-year-olds do not look old to me. I would estimate his age around 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the time when he took that child out of the hangar, did you see him in some other situations? Did he do anything else?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: He was there all the time. He was there, together with a major. I can't say that he did anything particular apart from saving that child. They looked as if they had a supervisory role in that whole story.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go back to Sremska Mitrovica. I read your earlier statements and your testimony, and I did not notice that you had mentioned before this delegation from Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and the arrival of Goran Hadzic at Sremska Mitrovica. Could you just explain how come that you mention it now? In fact, not now. You told the Prosecutor about it last summer.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: If you have read my statements, you will notice that I said very little about Velepromet and very little about Sremska Mitrovica. The reason was that I am supposed to talk in court only about the things they ask me. I can't tell my whole story from beginning to end. That's the reason why I just skimmed over Velepromet and Sremska Mitrovica both.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be all. Thank you, Mr. Karlovic.

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Stringer, anything in re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No -- no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, this is the end of your testimony. We thank you for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal, even in these circumstances. You're now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey back to your country. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish all the best to all of you too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If there's nothing else, court adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.54 a.m.
